# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

# gh-1439 rework — CI quality gates fixed

## Issues/Notes

Validation CI on head `358726a` was red. The "Quality gate" failure was only
the aggregate — the single real red leg was **"CRAP + duplication"**

Three concrete violations, all introduced by the gh-1439 changes to
`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`:

1. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel._handleMouseWheel` measured **16.00**
   (CC 8 @ 87.5% branch coverage) against the repo-pinned threshold 12.0.
   On `main` the same method is CC 6 → CRAP 10.50. The PR's new
   wheel-as-page-gesture `switch` added two decision points without adding
   coverage.
2. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel.view` measured **13.00** (CC 13 @ 100%
   coverage) vs **11.00** (CC 11) on `main`. The new jump-chip hit-region
   guard (`!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`) added two decision points
   inline in the already-CC-11 frame builder.
3. **loc gate (hidden)** — `crap4dart check --baseline` (the step *after*
   the CRAP step, which never executed on the red head) fails with
   `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart: 2812 lines > max 2800`. Main sits at 2742;
   the PR's +70 lines busted the whole-tree ≤2800 file cap.

Mid-rework, the branch automation merged fresh `main` (gh-1433) into the PR
branch, which re-inflated `fa_tui.dart` to 2825 lines — the loc shave below
accounts for that merge. The same automation had also swept a local
coverage scratch run (`coverage-verify/`, 47 `.vm.json` artifacts) onto the

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the

  0.11.0 over coverage from the wheel-touching suites —

  head**, byte-identical to CI; `view` CC 11 → 13; `check --baseline`
  → `[FAIL] loc: 2812 > 2800`.
- **GREEN (fix)**:
  - Split `_handleMouseWheel` into a 3-way dispatcher and moved the trio to
    the `_TuiViewport` extension in `fa_tui_viewport.dart` (a `part of`
    file — the same split-out convention the file itself documents for the
    2800-line gate): `_handleMouseWheel` (route only), `_wheelToHubSelection`
    (the pre-existing overlay half, unchanged behavior) and
    `_wheelTranscript` (the gh-1439 page gesture, unchanged behavior).

    and the `default:` no-op.

    `_registerJumpLiveRegion(stickyRows, historyRows)` with the identical
    predicate (De Morgan of `!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`); the click
    path (`TuiRegionKind.jumpLive` → `_jumpToLive()`) is untouched.

    `_registerJumpLiveRegion` also moved into the `_TuiViewport` extension:
    `fa_tui.dart` is now **2786 lines** (< 2800, was 2812 pre-merge /
    2825 post-merge).

  extracted halves)**:
  - `test/cli/fa_tui_mouse_test.dart`: new group pinning the hub-overlay
    wheel contract — wheel steps the fleet-tree selection and never moves
    the transcript offset or the follow state; plus REG tests that a
    `MouseWheelMsg` carrying a non-wheel button is a no-op both under the

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

# gh-1439 rework — CI quality gates fixed

## Issues/Notes

Validation CI on head `358726a` was red. The "Quality gate" failure was only
the aggregate — the single real red leg was **"CRAP + duplication"**
(`guards`), and it was hiding a second, not-yet-run gate failure behind it.
Three concrete violations, all introduced by the gh-1439 changes to
`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`:

1. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel._handleMouseWheel` measured **16.00**
   (CC 8 @ 87.5% branch coverage) against the repo-pinned threshold 12.0.
   On `main` the same method is CC 6 → CRAP 10.50. The PR's new
   wheel-as-page-gesture `switch` added two decision points without adding
   coverage.
2. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel.view` measured **13.00** (CC 13 @ 100%
   coverage) vs **11.00** (CC 11) on `main`. The new jump-chip hit-region
   guard (`!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`) added two decision points
   inline in the already-CC-11 frame builder.
3. **loc gate (hidden)** — `crap4dart check --baseline` (the step *after*
   the CRAP step, which never executed on the red head) fails with
   `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart: 2812 lines > max 2800`. Main sits at 2742;
   the PR's +70 lines busted the whole-tree ≤2800 file cap.

Mid-rework, the branch automation merged fresh `main` (gh-1433) into the PR
branch, which re-inflated `fa_tui.dart` to 2825 lines — the loc shave below
accounts for that merge. The same automation had also swept a local
coverage scratch run (`coverage-verify/`, 47 `.vm.json` artifacts) onto the
branch; those are untracked again and the path is now gitignored (the
gh-1033 sweep precedent).

Everything else on the failed run was green (core shards, fa_ui, PTY IT,
visual, static, flutter-analyze). No review threads were open, so there are
no threaded replies.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:

- **RED (reproduce)**: reproduced the CI numbers locally with crap4dart
  0.11.0 over coverage from the wheel-touching suites —
  `_handleMouseWheel` **10.50 (CC 6) on `origin/main` → 16.00 (CC 8) on
  head**, byte-identical to CI; `view` CC 11 → 13; `check --baseline`
  → `[FAIL] loc: 2812 > 2800`.
- **GREEN (fix)**:
  - Split `_handleMouseWheel` into a 3-way dispatcher and moved the trio to
    the `_TuiViewport` extension in `fa_tui_viewport.dart` (a `part of`
    file — the same split-out convention the file itself documents for the
    2800-line gate): `_handleMouseWheel` (route only), `_wheelToHubSelection`
    (the pre-existing overlay half, unchanged behavior) and
    `_wheelTranscript` (the gh-1439 page gesture, unchanged behavior).
    Behavior is byte-for-byte identical — including the `delta == 0` no-op
    and the `default:` no-op.
  - Extracted the jump-chip guard from `view()` into
    `_registerJumpLiveRegion(stickyRows, historyRows)` with the identical
    predicate (De Morgan of `!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`); the click
    path (`TuiRegionKind.jumpLive` → `_jumpToLive()`) is untouched.
  - After the gh-1433 merge re-inflated the file, `_handleWindowSize` and
    `_registerJumpLiveRegion` also moved into the `_TuiViewport` extension:
    `fa_tui.dart` is now **2786 lines** (< 2800, was 2812 pre-merge /
    2825 post-merge).
- **Tests (REG + coverage, per the repo precedent of covering the newly
  extracted halves)**:
  - `test/cli/fa_tui_mouse_test.dart`: new group pinning the hub-overlay
    wheel contract — wheel steps the fleet-tree selection and never moves
    the transcript offset or the follow state; plus REG tests that a
    `MouseWheelMsg` carrying a non-wheel button is a no-op both under the
    hub and on the transcript (they cover the extracted helpers' `default`
    legs end-to-end).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui_viewport.dart` — `_handleMouseWheel` moved here from
  `fa_tui.dart` and split into `_handleMouseWheel` /
  `_wheelToHubSelection` / `_wheelTranscript` (behavior-identical);
  `_handleWindowSize` and `_registerJumpLiveRegion` moved here after the
  gh-1433 merge re-inflated the model file.
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart` — jump-chip registration extracted from
  `view()` into `_registerJumpLiveRegion`; wheel/resize handlers moved to
  the viewport part file. 2812 → **2786 lines**.
- `test/cli/fa_tui_mouse_test.dart` — hub-wheel REG group (selection steps,
  transcript/follow untouched) + non-wheel-button no-op REG tests for both
  wheel halves.
- `.gitignore` — `coverage-verify/` added to the coverage-scratch ignore
  class (gh-1033 precedent); the 47 swept `.vm.json` artifacts untracked.

## Test Coverage

- Reproduced gate numbers before the fix (crap4dart 0.11.0, same coverage
  source as CI): `_handleMouseWheel` 16.00 / `view` CC 13 / loc 2812 —

- Full core suite + gates on the final tree: `dart test

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

## Approach

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:

- **RED (reproduce)**: reproduced the CI numbers locally with crap4dart

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

   coverage.

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

# gh-1439 rework — CI quality gates fixed

Validation CI on head `358726a` was red. The "Quality gate" failure was only
the aggregate — the single real red leg was **"CRAP + duplication"**
(`guards`), and it was hiding a second, not-yet-run gate failure behind it.
Three concrete violations, all introduced by the gh-1439 changes to
`lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`:

1. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel._handleMouseWheel` measured **16.00**

   coverage.
2. **CRAP ratchet** — `FaTuiModel.view` measured **13.00** (CC 13 @ 100%
   coverage) vs **11.00** (CC 11) on `main`. The new jump-chip hit-region
   guard (`!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`) added two decision points

3. **loc gate (hidden)** — `crap4dart check --baseline` (the step *after*

branch, which re-inflated `fa_tui.dart` to 2825 lines — the loc shave below
accounts for that merge. The same automation had also swept a local
coverage scratch run (`coverage-verify/`, 47 `.vm.json` artifacts) onto the
branch; those are untracked again and the path is now gitignored (the
gh-1033 sweep precedent).

Everything else on the failed run was green (core shards, fa_ui, PTY IT,
visual, static, flutter-analyze). No review threads were open, so there are
no threaded replies.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:

- **RED (reproduce)**: reproduced the CI numbers locally with crap4dart
  0.11.0 over coverage from the wheel-touching suites —
  `_handleMouseWheel` **10.50 (CC 6) on `origin/main` → 16.00 (CC 8) on
  head**, byte-identical to CI; `view` CC 11 → 13; `check --baseline`
  → `[FAIL] loc: 2812 > 2800`.
- **GREEN (fix)**:
  - Split `_handleMouseWheel` into a 3-way dispatcher and moved the trio to
    the `_TuiViewport` extension in `fa_tui_viewport.dart` (a `part of`
    file — the same split-out convention the file itself documents for the
    2800-line gate): `_handleMouseWheel` (route only), `_wheelToHubSelection`

    `_wheelTranscript` (the gh-1439 page gesture, unchanged behavior).

    and the `default:` no-op.
  - Extracted the jump-chip guard from `view()` into
    `_registerJumpLiveRegion(stickyRows, historyRows)` with the identical
    predicate (De Morgan of `!followTail && follow.unseen > 0`); the click
    path (`TuiRegionKind.jumpLive` → `_jumpToLive()`) is untouched.

    `_registerJumpLiveRegion` also moved into the `_TuiViewport` extension:
    `fa_tui.dart` is now **2786 lines** (< 2800, was 2812 pre-merge /
    2825 post-merge).
- **Tests (REG + coverage, per the repo precedent of covering the newly
  extracted halves)**:

    wheel contract — wheel steps the fleet-tree selection and never moves

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

Closes #1439
### What changed
- New core `FollowMode` value type (`lib/src/viewport/follow_mode.dart`, new `── viewport ──` barrel group): the single owner of live/held state + unseen count, shared by the TUI and the Flutter app (AC3).

- Follow semantics live once in core and are unit-tested there; both surfaces only translate gestures into `userScrolled`/`appended`/`jumpToLive` calls.
- Unseen accounting rides `FollowMode.appended()` — a held window never auto-moves (E1/E2), arrivals only increment the counter.
- REG: the `#827` live-fold hint, `#1159` banner and `#379` clamp contracts are pinned by untouched suites (all green).

```bash

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:
