blocks.text:
# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

blocks.text:
# gh-1439: [GOAL] Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (TUI + app + web: follow-mode contract + «jump to live» affordance)

## Description

## Goal — Live-follow etiquette: scrolling up while the agent works never yanks the user back down (v1)

One sentence: **While Fa is producing output, a user who scrolls up to read history STAYS there on every surface (CLI TUI, app, web), and a one-action «jump to live» affordance brings them back when they choose.**

Today every surface auto-follows the stream unconditionally: new deltas, tool cards, and settle cards force the transcript viewport to the bottom, so reading back during a run is impossible — the view jumps under the user on every event (owner report, #1439). The TUI already has a scroll fold (`────^ 8 lines above fold -PgUp────`) and the app has a lazy «Load newer (N more)» banner (#135, #1159) — the missing piece is a **follow-mode contract**: scrolling up disengages auto-follow, output keeps arriving (counted, not shown by force), and an explicit affordance (chip/button/key) re-engages.

## Why this framing

- Not «add a scroll-to-bottom button» — the BUTTON is the small half; the contract (auto-follow disengage/re-engage) is the capability, and it must behave the SAME on all three faces.
- Not a transcript redesign: the transcript widgets stay as they are; this card owns the viewport-follow policy layer above them.
- Supersedes the implicit assumption «streaming ⇒ always bottom-anchored» — that assumption predates long agentic runs where reading back mid-run is the norm.

## Architecture

**FollowMode** (per viewport, pure state): `live` (auto-follow on) ⇄ `held` (user scrolled up; output appended, viewport anchored) — with a counted `unseenDelta` while held.

```
stream event → transcript append ──→ viewport
                     │                 ├─ FollowMode.live  → scroll to bottom (today's behavior)
                     │                 └─ FollowMode.held  → viewport stays; unseen++ → affordance shows
user input ──→ PgUp/wheel-up/drag-up → held
            ──→ End/jump-chip/button/gesture-scroll-to-bottom → live (+flush unseen)
```

Invariants:
- **Zero output loss**: held mode appends everything to the model; only the VIEWPORT withholds.
- **Re-engage is always exactly one action** on every surface and is visible whenever `unseen > 0` (no hidden keys).
- **Near-bottom re-arm**: a user scroll that lands within the bottom N px/rows of the newest content re-engages `live` automatically (the standard chat heuristic) — no button press needed for the common «scroll down to catch up» case.
- Resume/boot always starts `live` at the newest record (lazy history loads OLDER, #135 — unchanged).

## Capability surface

| face | disengage trigger | re-engage action | affordance while held |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI TUI | PgUp/PgDn/wheel-up (mouse capture modes), any fold expand | `End`/`G`, wheel-to-bottom, PgDn past newest, on-screen jump chip | fold indicator GROWS a «● N new» live counter next to the existing `-PgUp` fold line |
| App (iOS/Android/desktop) | drag-up with momentum, trackpad wheel-up, keyboard PgUp (desktop) | tap the jump chip, drag-to-bottom (near-bottom re-arm), hardware End where present | floating «⌄ N new» pill above the composer (same slot family as the #1159 banner, but live-updating) |
| Web (app-on-web + demo) | wheel-up/scroll-up | click the pill, near-bottom re-arm | same pill, mouse-cursor friendly hit area |
| wire/serve read-only viewers | n/a (no input) | n/a | excluded — display-only surfaces keep today's behavior |

**Core**: FollowMode + disengage/re-engage + jump affordance with live unseen counter + near-bottom re-arm, on TUI + app + web. **Second tier**: unseen-content category hints (chip distinguishes «N new» vs «agent replied» vs «needs approval» — approval prompts must ALSO surface through the chip, see E6); per-surface follow-mode persistence in session prefs. **Excluded** (rationale): transcript search/highlight (trajectory family owns it), changing the lazy pagination contract (#135 pin), read-only wire viewers (no viewport input path).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — TUI: during a streaming run (fake model), PgUp holds the fold position through ≥50 subsequent append events; the fold line shows the live `● N new` counter; `End`/jump-chip returns to live and flushes N. PTY IT.
- **AC2** — App: widget test — drag-up during a streaming run pins the list; the pill shows the count; tap jumps to bottom; near-bottom drag re-arms live without the pill.
- **AC3** — Web: same contract as AC2 in the web harness (shared widget path — assert the shared FollowMode owner, not a copy).
- **AC4** — Zero loss: after a held-mode session, the rendered transcript (post re-engage) contains every record the live mode would show (property test against a twin live run).
- **AC5** — Boot/resume starts `live` at newest; held state never persists across restarts.
- **AC6** — Approval prompts during held mode: the waiting-approval row still renders/escalates per its own rules — follow mode never delays or hides an approval prompt (the chip may badge «needs you», second tier).

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-*` FollowMode pure state machine (disengage/re-arm thresholds, unseen counting, flush).
- `IT-*` PTY TUI (AC1) with scripted stream + injected keys; app widget tests (AC2); web harness smoke (AC3) — mocked LLM throughout (FakeStreamFunction / fake agent), no network.
- `E2E-*` Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) golden: held fold + counter chip during a scripted run.
- `REG-*` today's behavior pins: no user scroll ⇒ byte-identical auto-follow output; #1159 banner contract untouched; #135 lazy pagination untouched. **A red REG blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — compaction fold / checkpoint rebuild re-rendering the transcript while held: viewport anchor survives (anchored to record id, not pixel offset).
- **E2** — resize mid-hold (TUI and app): anchor recomputes to the same logical position.
- **E3** — image blocks / generated-image previews arriving while held: counted in unseen, rendered on re-engage, never force-scroll.
- **E4** — huge backlog held (lazy #135): jumping to live does not load the entire history — it lands at the newest window.
- **E5** — steering notice / settle cards while held: same as any append (counted, no yank).
- **E6** — approval prompt while held (see AC6) and near-bottom re-arm racing a burst of appends (debounce: re-arm wins only when the user gesture, not the stream, produced the position).
- **E7** — mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE) interacting with wheel-up: disengage works in captured AND native-selection modes (native mode disengages only on explicit PgUp — documented).

## Non-goals

- No transcript chrome redesign, no search, no change to lazy pagination (#135) or the #1159 banner semantics (the pill is a SIBLING surface, not a rework of it).
- No persistence of held state; no multi-viewport sync (wire viewers excluded).

## Open questions

1. Near-bottom re-arm threshold: rows (TUI) vs px (app) — pick a per-surface constant or a shared fraction of viewport height? Leaning: fraction (~10%).
2. Chip content: bare counter `⌄ 42` vs categorized badge (second tier) — ship the bare counter first?
3. TUI jump affordance placement: extend the existing fold line (`-PgUp` gets `· End = live`) vs a separate status-bar segment? Leaning: fold line extension — zero new chrome.

## References

- Owner report (this issue). #135 (lazy session rendering — the pagination this must not disturb), #1159 (Load-newer banner precedent + its isStreaming guard lesson), TUI fold indicator (`-PgUp` line), mouse-mode auto-detect (FA_TUI_MOUSE / `/mouse`), PTY screenshot E2E family (Terminal visual jobs).

## Approach

Followed the repo's established CRAP-repair pattern (pure extraction of
cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the
#1234 offenders), verified with a controlled measurement before/after:

- **RED (reproduce)**: reproduced the CI numbers locally with crap4dart

    `_registerJumpLiveRegion` also moved into the `_TuiViewport` extension:

cohesive sub-dispatchers — the same move `crap4dart.yaml` documents for the

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

Golden tests are mandatory for `flutter_app/lib/` UI work. The PR changed `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart` (the fa_ui package, used by flutter_app and web demo). Is `packages/fa_ui` covered by the golden-test mandate? The mandate says "flutter_app/lib/ UI code". The fa_ui package is a separate package (packages/fa_ui). ## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
